plain_english: What you see here is the best rule we found by searching, not a rule that has passed an independent test. We tried 4,396 valid strategy combinations on data the models had not seen, and this one came out on top (Sharpe 1.50 vs 0.89 for simply buying and holding SPY). But three honesty checks temper that: (1) the typical strategy in our search scored only 0.74 — WORSE than buy-and-hold — so the search mostly found ways to lose, and the winner may simply be the luckiest of thousands of tries; (2) a statistical re-shuffle test says a result this good could happen by chance about 6.6% of the time (we want under 5% before calling it real); (3) the rule looked unimpressive on older data (Sharpe 0.35 before 2018), its edge is concentrated in one episode (the COVID crash), the signal's relationship with the market flips sign frequently over time, and it sits in cash 75% of the time — most of its advantage is simply avoiding losses, not picking winners. Bigger picture: business loans are a LAGGING indicator — the stock market moves first and loan books respond afterward — so this is best read as a defensive 'stay out when credit is behaving oddly' overlay found by search, NOT a validated forecasting signal. No fresh confirmation test (final exam) on held-out data has been run yet.
